beats.care: Less dumped debris means less dust on the roads you walk and ride on, especially near building sites.
beats.what: BMC now fines vehicles carrying construction or excavation waste Rs 25,000 if they lack an active tracking device.
beats.why: Illegally dumped debris adds to dust and pollution. Tracking shows where each load actually ends up.

cards.body: Between Aug 24 and Oct 10 on its debris tracking portal, a senior BMC official said.
cards.caption: registrations on BMC's portal

cards.body: Developers and transporters must register on BMC's Mumbai Debris Control & Tracking System portal, launched Aug 24. About 128 developers covering 250–300 sites have signed up.

cards.q: Will a fine stop illegal dumping?

opts: It shows where each truck actually unloads
It bans trucks from the city
cards.q: How does GPS tracking help cut illegal debris dumping?
cards.why: With live tracking, BMC can see if a load goes to an approved site or gets dumped elsewhere.

hook: Why is BMC tracking *debris trucks* by GPS now?

learn.t: Mumbai produces nearly 8,000 tonnes of construction and demolition waste every single day.

sources.name: Social News XYZ
sources.title: BMC to crack down on illegal debris disposal, impose Rs 25,000 fine for tracking violations

tldr: From October 12, BMC fines debris trucks Rs 25,000 per offence if they run without an active GPS tracking device.
